drill.titleSentence: Dates and times in a sentence
drills.genderChen: Diminutives ending in -chen and -lein are always neuter.
drills.genderDays: Days, months and seasons are masculine.
drills.genderE: Most nouns ending in -e are feminine (about nine in ten).
drills.genderGe: Many nouns starting with Ge- are neuter (das Gebäude, das Gemüse).
drills.genderIn: Female forms ending in -in are feminine (die Lehrerin).
drills.genderLing: Nouns ending in -ling, -ismus, -or, -ist and -ant are masculine.
drills.genderMent: Nouns ending in -ment, -um and -ma are usually neuter.
drills.hintArticleDefault: Learn every noun together with its article: the article is part of the word.
drills.hintAuxSein: {verb} takes "sein": movement from A to B or a change of state.
drills.hintAuxVaries: {verb} takes "sein" for movement (ist gefahren) and "haben" with an object (hat das Auto gefahren).
drills.hintClock: Formal: hour + "Uhr" + minutes (24-hour clock). Everyday: "nach", "vor", "halb" (half TO the next hour), "Viertel".
drills.hintCompound: A compound takes the gender of its last part: {last} → {whole}.
drills.hintDate: Ordinal + month: "der {ordinal} …" after "Heute ist", "am {ordinal}n …" after "am". Month {month} = {monthDe}.
drills.hintMeaningDefault: Think of a sentence you would use it in.
drills.hintNumber: Units before tens, joined with "und": {pieces}. One word, no spaces.
drills.hintOrdinal: Ordinals 1-19 end in -te (erste, dritte, siebte, achte are irregular), from 20 in -ste; after "am" add -n.
drills.hintPreterite: Irregular verbs change their stem in the Präteritum: {infinitive} → {preterite}.
drills.hintPrice: Euros first, then the cents, usually without "Cent": "drei Euro vierzig".
drills.instrClock: Say the time in German. Formal or everyday both count.
drills.instrDate: Say the date in words, as in "Heute ist …" or "am …".
drills.instrPrice: The cashier reads the price aloud. Write what they say.
drills.instrSentence: Translate. Write the date and the time in words.
drills.numberHundreds: hundreds and thousands come first, all in one word
drills.pluralDie: The plural always takes "die", whatever the gender.
drills.pluralE: Many masculine nouns add -e in the plural.
drills.pluralEUmlaut: This one adds -e and an umlaut, like der Stuhl → die Stühle.
drills.pluralErUmlaut: This one adds -er and an umlaut, like das Haus → die Häuser.
drills.pluralFeminine: Feminine nouns usually add -n or -en in the plural.
drills.pluralS: Words from English and French, and words ending in a vowel, often add -s.
drills.pluralSame: Masculine and neuter nouns ending in -er, -el and -en often stay the same in the plural.
